title: Generator presentation and its transported partial-adjoint relation
statement: Let $\mathcal A,\mathcal B$ be abelian categories [def-sp-abelian] and let $R:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ be additive [def-weil-pbc-additive-functor]. Let $\mathcal P\subset\operatorname{Ob}(\mathcal B)$ satisfy: every object of $\mathcal B$ admits an epimorphism from an object of $\mathcal P$. For each $P\in\mathcal P$, fix $L_P\in\mathcal A$ and bijections $\theta_{P,X}:\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal A}(L_P,X)\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal B}(P,R(X))$ natural in $X$, meaning $\theta_{P,X'}(u\circ a)=R(u)\circ\theta_{P,X}(a)$ for $u:X\to X'$. Put $i_P=\theta_{P,L_P}(\mathrm{id}_{L_P})$. Then $\theta_{P,X}(a)=R(a)\circ i_P$ and $\theta_{P,X}(0)=0$ for every $P,X,a$. For every $B\in\mathcal B$ there exist $P_1,P_2\in\mathcal P$, epimorphisms $q:P_1\twoheadrightarrow B$ and $r:P_2\twoheadrightarrow K$, and a kernel $k:K\to P_1$ of $q$, such that, on putting $d=k\circ r$, the map $q$ is a cokernel of $d$: $q\circ d=0$, and every $h:P_1\to Y$ with $h\circ d=0$ factors uniquely as $h=b\circ q$. For these choices there is a unique $D:L_{P_2}\to L_{P_1}$ with $\theta_{P_2,L_{P_1}}(D)=i_{P_1}\circ d$. For every $X\in\mathcal A$ and $a:L_{P_1}\to X$, it satisfies $\theta_{P_2,X}(a\circ D)=\theta_{P_1,X}(a)\circ d$, and consequently $a\circ D=0$ if and only if $\theta_{P_1,X}(a)\circ d=0$.

source.place: Tag 0793, lemma-partially-defined-adjoint, proof: first paragraph and the choice of an exact presentation in the second paragraph; additive specialization.

proof.text: Apply the stipulated naturality with $a=\mathrm{id}_{L_P}$ and $u:L_P\to X$. This gives $\theta_{P,X}(u)=R(u)\circ i_P$. By [def-weil-pbc-additive-functor], the map on each Hom group is a group homomorphism, so $R(0)=0$. Taking $u=0$ in the formula gives $\theta_{P,X}(0)=0\circ i_P=0$.

source.place: Tag 0793, lemma-partially-defined-adjoint, proof, first paragraph (evaluation at the identity and induced map) and second paragraph (choice of exact presentation); additive specialization. Tag 0109, definition-abelian-category, supplies the abelian axioms.

proof.text: For $B\in\mathcal B$, use the covering hypothesis to choose $P_1\in\mathcal P$ and an epimorphism $q:P_1\to B$. Kernels exist by [def-sp-abelian]; choose a kernel $k:K\to P_1$ of $q$. Apply the same covering hypothesis to $K$ to choose $P_2\in\mathcal P$ and an epimorphism $r:P_2\to K$. Set $d=k\circ r$. The kernel identity gives $q\circ d=(q\circ k)\circ r=0$.

source.place: Tag 0793, lemma-partially-defined-adjoint, proof, first paragraph (evaluation at the identity and induced map) and second paragraph (choice of exact presentation); additive specialization. Tag 0109, definition-abelian-category, supplies the abelian axioms.

proof.text: By [def-sp-abelian], the epimorphism $q$ is a cokernel of some $t:T\to P_1$. Since $q\circ t=0$, the universal property of the chosen kernel gives $s:T\to K$ with $t=k\circ s$. If $h:P_1\to Y$ satisfies $h\circ d=0$, then $(h\circ k)\circ r=0\circ r$; cancellation of the epimorphism $r$ gives $h\circ k=0$. Hence $h\circ t=(h\circ k)\circ s=0$. The cokernel property of $q$ for $t$ supplies a unique $b:B\to Y$ with $h=b\circ q$. Together with step 2 this is exactly the cokernel property of $q$ for $d$.

source.place: Tag 0793, lemma-partially-defined-adjoint, proof, first paragraph (evaluation at the identity and induced map) and second paragraph (choice of exact presentation); additive specialization. Tag 0109, definition-abelian-category, supplies the abelian axioms.

proof.text: The composite $i_{P_1}\circ d$ lies in $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal B}(P_2,R(L_{P_1}))$. Define $D=\theta_{P_2,L_{P_1}}^{-1}(i_{P_1}\circ d)$. Bijectivity gives both its stated defining equation and uniqueness. For $a:L_{P_1}\to X$, the given naturality and step 1 give $\theta_{P_2,X}(a\circ D)=R(a)\circ\theta_{P_2,L_{P_1}}(D)=R(a)\circ i_{P_1}\circ d=\theta_{P_1,X}(a)\circ d$.

source.place: Tag 0793, lemma-partially-defined-adjoint, proof, first paragraph (evaluation at the identity and induced map) and second paragraph (choice of exact presentation); additive specialization. Tag 0109, definition-abelian-category, supplies the abelian axioms.

proof.text: By step 1, $\theta_{P_2,X}(0)=0$. If $a\circ D=0$, step 4 therefore gives $\theta_{P_1,X}(a)\circ d=0$. Conversely, if the latter composite is zero, step 4 gives $\theta_{P_2,X}(a\circ D)=0=\theta_{P_2,X}(0)$, and injectivity of this bijection gives $a\circ D=0$.
